key_insight: GRADE is the first benchmark to evaluate discipline-informed knowledge and reasoning in image editing, using curated, domain-specific editing tasks to reveal gaps that commonsense-focused benchmarks miss.
problem_solved: Existing image-editing benchmarks focus on natural images and shallow commonsense reasoning, failing to assess models' ability to respect structured, domain-specific constraints needed for scientific and academic image edits.
method: Constructed GRADE: 520 carefully curated editing samples spanning 10 academic domains with domain-specific instructions and expert annotations.
Defined standardized evaluation protocols and metrics that measure discipline-informed correctness, constraint satisfaction, and visual fidelity.
Benchmarked leading unified multimodal/image-editing models to quantify capability gaps and common failure modes under structured domain constraints.
impact: GRADE gives AI/ML practitioners a targeted tool to diagnose and improve multimodal models' domain-aware editing abilities, informing dataset design, fine-tuning strategies, and safety checks for scientific/technical applications.
visual_elements: Dataset composition pie chart: 10 academic domains with sample counts and example thumbnails
Before/after edit triplets: original image, domain-specific instruction, and edited output for representative tasks
Performance bar chart or leaderboard: baseline model scores across discipline-informed metrics
Error analysis heatmap: common failure modes by domain and metric (e.g., constraint violation, visual artifacts)
paper_title: GRADE: Benchmarking Discipline-Informed Reasoning in Image Editing
paper_authors: Mingxin Liu, Ziqian Fan, Zhaokai Wang, Leyao Gu, Zirun Zhu
